perf.summary: relation[x*n+y] index recomputes x*n each j; the column index y is fixed per outer i, so hoist y and stride relation by rows or precompute base.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop computes `relation[x*n + y]` with x varying and y fixed — the multiply x*n happens per element, and the access pattern is column-major (stride n) over the relation matrix, causing a cache miss roughly every element for large n.
perf.proposedChange: Since y is fixed in the inner loop, the natural fix is to store/access relation transposed for this kernel (relation[y_row * n + x] = 'x relates to y') so the inner loop walks a contiguous row relation[y*n + ...], turning stride-n column access into stride-1. If the matrix layout is fixed, at minimum hoist `int yn = y` and rely on x*n; but the cache win requires the transposed access. Also the `relation` bool* could be a bitset to cut the working set 8x.
perf.rationale: Column-major bool access at stride n thrashes cache for n beyond a few hundred; a contiguous row walk is the single biggest real-world speedup here. A bitset packs 64 relations per long, shrinking the matrix from n^2 bytes to n^2/8 and improving cache residency dramatically.
perf.risk: Transposing relation changes the data contract with callers and with LatticeMeet/Join/MobiusTransform which also index relation[x*n+y] vs [z*n+x]; any layout change must be applied consistently across ALL users or it breaks correctness. Bitset packing changes the public signature (bool* -> ulong*). Treat as a coordinated refactor, not a local edit.

perf.summary: Zeroing the mu matrix uses `(long)n*n` recomputed in the loop condition and writes every cell though only the upper triangle is populated.
perf.currentCost: `for (int i=0; i<(long)n*n; i++)` recomputes n*n as a long each iteration (the compiler likely hoists it, but the long compare is wider than needed) and zeroes all n^2 entries even though only reachable (x,y) pairs are later set.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist `long total = (long)n*n;` before the loop (or use `int` since n^2 fits int for realistic n and is faster), and consider memset via Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned for the zero-fill rather than a scalar loop. The scalar zero loop is O(n^2) of pure stores — a block clear is far faster and Burst/JIT-friendly.
perf.rationale: Block-clearing n^2 longs with InitBlock is memory-bandwidth-bound and several times faster than a scalar store loop; hoisting the bound removes a redundant widening multiply per iteration.
perf.risk: InitBlock zeroes bytes — valid since 0L is all-zero bytes. If n^2 longs exceeds int range the byte count must stay long; for realistic poset sizes n^2 fits int comfortably. No semantic change.

perf.summary: Hand-rolled popcount loop can be replaced by the intrinsic / AggressiveInlining leaf.
perf.currentCost: `while(x>0){x&=x-1;c++;}` is a data-dependent loop of up to 32 iterations with an unpredictable trip count, where a single hardware POPCNT exists.
perf.proposedChange: Use System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)x) (Burst lowers to popcnt) or math.countbits in Unity.Mathematics. Mark the method [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]. Cast to uint to match the intended non-negative semantics.
perf.rationale: Replaces an up-to-32-iteration dependency chain with one instruction; Burst and modern CPUs have native popcount, eliminating the loop and its branch.
perf.risk: x is int; the current loop treats x as the bit pattern of the positive value (x>0 guard skips the sign bit case). PopCount((uint)x) counts all 32 bits including bit 31 — for x>=0 this matches exactly; for negative x the old loop's `x>0` would... actually `x&(x-1)` on negative x loops oddly. Confirm callers only pass non-negative x (lattice ranks are >=0); then (uint) cast is exact.

perf.summary: O(n^2) per query with column-stride relation access; minor hoist of x,y indices and early-exit already present.
perf.currentCost: For each candidate z, an inner w-loop scans n entries at stride n (relation[w*n+x]) — column-major, cache-unfriendly. Two such matrix reads per w.
perf.proposedChange: These are inherently O(n^2) per query. Cache benefit again comes from a transposed/bitset relation (see ZetaTransform note) so the w-loop is contiguous and can AND two bitset rows 64 lanes at a time, finding mismatches with a single masked compare instead of per-w branches.
perf.rationale: A bitset relation lets `relation_row_x & relation_row_y & ~relation_row_z == 0` be checked 64 elements per long, collapsing the inner n-loop by 64x and removing per-w branches.
perf.risk: Same coordinated-layout-change risk as the ZetaTransform bitset proposal; only worthwhile if the whole module adopts the packed representation. Otherwise leave as-is.
